text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Wednesday:
- Several companies have been accused of smuggling some 2,000 tons of vegetables into Switzerland from Italy between 1994 and 1996.
- Automobile sales in Switzerland fell by 6.5 percent in January to 19,479 compared to January 1996.
- Pharmaceuticals giant Novartis acquired U.S. biotechnology firm Systemix.
- Shoe manufacturer Bally will cut 20 of 230 jobs at its Schoenenwerd factory in an attempt to improve profitability. - Gewerbebank Zurich posted a net profit of 2.41 million Swiss francs for 1996.
- Six skiers died in avalanches in different areas of the Swiss Alps at the weekend.
- Josef Oberholzer, a bank executive at Union Bank of Switzerland, on trial in Zurich on charges of laundering drug money from Colombia, faces a possible 30-month prison sentence.
- Overnight stays in Swiss hotels fell by 4.8 percent to 29.73 million in 1996, the weakest result in 31 years.
- Lenzburg-based food and beverage group Hero is selling its British subsidiary Rayner, a producer of syrup, sauces and flavorings.
- Sects are very active in the health professions, according to a report issued by the Geneva justice and police department.
